name: AlloyDB for PostgreSQL
tagline: Google's Postgres-compatible service with disaggregated storage, a columnar engine and ScaNN vectors.
description: AlloyDB is Google Cloud's high-end PostgreSQL-compatible database. It keeps the Postgres query engine but moves storage into a regional, log-processing storage service, adds an automatically managed in-memory columnar engine for analytical queries, and ships ScaNN-based vector indexes and in-database model calls under the AlloyDB AI banner. AlloyDB Omni packages the same engine for self-managed deployment on any cloud, on-premises or Kubernetes. It suits teams on Google Cloud that need more throughput and faster mixed OLTP/analytics than Cloud SQL, and want to stay on real Postgres semantics; it is overkill and pricier for small databases.

license.name: Proprietary (Google Cloud service; AlloyDB Omni commercial license)

pricing.notes: Billed per vCPU/memory-hour and storage, with committed-use discounts; free trial clusters are time-limited; AlloyDB Omni has a free developer edition and paid production licensing.

scale.notes: Single primary with scalable read pools and cross-region secondary clusters; storage scales automatically.

strengths: Real PostgreSQL semantics, including PostgreSQL 18 compatibility (GA March 2026)
Adaptive in-memory columnar engine accelerates analytical queries without schema changes
ScaNN vector indexes and in-database Vertex AI model calls for RAG
AlloyDB Omni runs the same engine on any cloud, on-prem or Kubernetes
Federated queries into BigQuery via bigquery_fdw
weaknesses: Single writer; no built-in horizontal write sharding
More expensive than Cloud SQL for small or idle databases
Managed service is Google Cloud only
Proprietary storage layer means behavior differs from vanilla Postgres under some workloads
useCases: Migrating demanding Postgres or Oracle workloads to Google Cloud
Operational analytics on live transactional data
RAG and semantic search with vectors stored beside business data
Hybrid deployments using AlloyDB Omni on-premises
notIdealFor: Teams that must avoid cloud-specific Postgres forks
